reviews.author: Danny Kargar
reviews.text: We visited this Japanese restaurant on Saturday and, unfortunately, the service really let the experience down. The person who welcomed us when we arrived was very friendly and polite, which was a great first impression. However, the girl who took our order was quite rude and made us feel uncomfortable. The person who brought our food also had a very unpleasant attitude. What concerned us the most was the hygiene. While bringing food to our table, as well as serving other tables, the staff member repeatedly scratched himself. This was very off-putting and, in my opinion, is not appropriate when handling and serving food. The food itself was actually okay and we had no major complaints about the quality. However, when we visited on Saturday, we also wanted to order cocktails, but they didn't even have vodka available to make them, which was disappointing for a Saturday evening. Overall, the food was decent, but the service, attitude of some staff members, and especially the hygiene standards really need improvement. Unfortunately, these issues had a big impact on our overall experience.

reviews.author: Niamh Magee
reviews.text: Hugely disappointed by this place. It's got great reviews from friends, but I cannot see for the life of me why that would be. The food is extraordinarily bland - I went with a friend who got their spiciest dish and it had no spice to it whatsoever. I got the chicken ramen, and when it first arrived, the chicken was raw. The server explained that the pink colour I was noticing was because it was marinated in pink gin before it was cooked, but that they'd be happy to replace it. My second serving had the same issue. While it wasn't pink, it had the texture of severely undercooked chicken and was translucent in some areas (I've attached a photo, though it was more visible in person). Another server explained that this was due to it being chicken thigh, which makes it more "succulent". I've eaten a lot of chicken thigh in my life and it has never had that texture when cooked. Safe to say I didn't eat anything further. Every time a customer is seated, a staff member bangs a drum. This is weird, but amusing at first, but quickly becomes incredibly grating. The whole place is decorated like an overdone gimmick of Japan, making it feel more like a cheap Disney display than a comfortable place to eat. I was also disappointed to learn that the £5 ramen offer you get for downloading their app does not apply in this location for whatever reason. The staff were an absolute delight, and did not charge me for my disastrous meal. They are attentive and friendly, and I can only assume the failures of this place are due to it being a poorly managed chain.

reviews.author: Emre Yurttakalın
reviews.text: (Translated by Google) Located within the dynamic atmosphere of a shopping center in Edinburgh, Maki & Ramen greets you with a queue stretching for meters, requiring considerable patience. However, gastronomy enthusiasts know one thing well: places that live up to their waiting times offer a satisfying finale. Indeed, once we sat down and tasted our first bites, I can confidently say that every minute we waited was well worth it. The interior, blending the authentic texture of East Asia with modern elegance, transports you from Scotland to the mysterious and mystical streets of the Far East. When you add the team's practical, extremely efficient, friendly, and solution-oriented service to this captivating environment, the experience reaches a flawless rhythm. As for the flavors and cooking techniques, a perfect balance of mastery and consistency prevails on the plate. The main ingredient, the meaty ramen soup, was captivating with its deep and silky texture brought about by hours of slow-simmering bone broth. The meat inside, thanks to the marinade and the perfect cooking degree, was incredibly tender, melting in your mouth and falling apart into strands. On the sushi side, the freshness of the ingredients in the recipes and the ideal balance of vinegar and sugar in the rice were immediately noticeable. The Salmon Avocado Roll we experienced achieved a delicious harmony with the freshness of the salmon and the creamy texture of the avocado. The Salmon Panko Roll offered a wonderful textural contrast with its crispy panko coating being perfectly fried without absorbing oil; while the Steak Tataki, offered with a halal meat option, transformed into a flavor feast that broke the mold in sushi with the degree to which the outside of the meat was seared and the inside was juicy and tender. In short, if you want to embark on a Far Eastern culinary journey with deep ramen and fresh sushi varieties prepared with the right cooking techniques, even if you are willing to wait in line during your trip to Edinburgh, Maki & Ramen is definitely a stop not to be missed. (Original) Edinburgh’da bir alışveriş merkezinin dinamik atmosferi içinde yer alan Maki & Ramen, kapısında metrelerce uzayan ve ciddi sabır gerektiren bir kuyrukla sizi karşılıyor. Ancak gastronomi tutkunlarının iyi bildigi bir gerçek vardır ki, o da kapısındaki sıranın hakkını veren mekanların sunduğu o tatmin edici finaldir. Nitekim masaya oturup ilk lokmaları tattığımızda, beklediğimiz her dakikaya sonuna kadar değdiğini gönül rahatlığıyla söyleyebilirim. Doğu Asya’nın otantik dokusunu modern bir zarafetle harmanlayan iç atmosferi, sizi adeta İskoçya’dan alıp Uzak Doğu’nun gizemli ve mistik sokaklarına götürüyor. Bu büyüleyici ortama, ekibin pratik, son derece seri, güler yüzlü ve çözüm odaklı hizmet anlayışı da eklenince deneyim kusursuz bir ritme kavuşuyor. Mutfaktan çıkan lezzetlere ve pişirme tekniklerine gelince; tabağa tam anlamıyla bir ustalık ve kıvam dengesi hakim. Ana rolü üstlenen etli ramen çorbası, saatlerce ağır ağır demlenmiş kemik suyunun getirdiği derin ve ipeksi kıvamıyla büyüleyiciydi. İçindeki etler ise marinasyonun ve doğru pişirme derecesinin hakkını vererek lif lif ayrılan, ağızda adeta eriyen muazzam bir yumuşaklığa sahipti. Sushi tarafında ise reçetelerdeki malzeme tazeliği ve pirincin sirke-şeker dengesindeki ideal kıvam hemen göze çarpıyordu. Deneyimlediğimiz Salmon Avocado Roll, somonun tazeliği ve avokadonun kremsi dokusuyla nefis bir uyum yakalamış. Salmon Panko Roll, dışındaki çıtır panko kaplamasının yağ çekmeden tam kıvamında kızartılmasıyla harika bir doku kontrastı sunarken; helal et seçeneğiyle sunulan Steak Tataki ise etin dış yüzeyinin mühürlenme derecesi ve içinin o sulu, yumuşak yapısıyla sushide ezber bozan bir lezzet şölenine dönüştü. Özetle; Edinburgh seyahatinizde sıra beklemeyi göze alarak, doğru pişirme teknikleriyle hazırlanmış derinlikli bir ramen ve taptaze sushi çeşitleriyle Uzak Doğu lezzet yolculuğuna çıkmak istiyorsanız, Maki & Ramen kesinlikle kaçırılmaması gereken bir durak.

reviews.text: Absolutely love Maki & Ramen! The food somehow tastes even better every single time I visit. Every time I try something new, I end up thinking I’ve found a new favourite! 😂 I’ve been to a few of their other locations, but the Aberdeen branch genuinely deserves an award for their customer service. The staff are always so friendly, attentive and welcoming, and the service is incredibly fast without compromising on the quality of the food. Everything is consistently delicious, the service is excellent, and you can really tell that the team cares about giving customers a great experience. Maki & Ramen Aberdeen never disappoints. Visited today and had such a lovely time. The food was honestly so good, as always, and the service was just as good. Jezer at the bar, Ian, Josephine, Peter the new supervisor and Abigail were all so lovely and attentive. You can really tell the team puts effort into making people feel welcome. The Aberdeen team genuinely deserves so much praise for how friendly, efficient and consistent they are. ❤️

reviews.author: Scott Lynch
reviews.text: Visited 26/09/26 Fantastic service - Manager and Barman looked after us very well - our table was in front of the bar. Very nice wine glasses. Amazing Chicken Green Curry Ramen! It's been on the menu since July 26' I understand and is a Thai-inspired green curry chicken broth with Sous vide chicken, pak choi, and a half soft-boiled egg with handcrafted noodles. I've been telling everyone how good it is! Everything was very clean. When you pay similar or more for a burger and chips in a restaurant, this is great value for money given the taste and quality. Looking forward to my next visit! For note - They hit the drum/gong on everyone's arrival - banging the large Taiko drum is a traditional way to welcome guests into the restaurant and create a lively, energetic atmosphere. In turn the staff shout “Irasshaimase!”, which is the traditional Japanese greeting meaning “welcome, come in". Learn something new everyday..

reviews.text: I don’t really understand the hype about Maki&Ramen unfortunately. I’ve been there 2x now thanks to freshers vouchers and none of the ramens I’ve tried has tasted good or authentic. I’ve tried the Chicken green curry ramen, steak tataki ramen, and vegan black garlic ramen. All of them had a dirty, gristly taste… like the char off a grill. The chicken in the ramen tasted freezer burnt and the vegan bacon had an aftertaste of burnt tires… very strange. I was excited to try this place since people seem to like it but I wouldn’t recommend the ramen. I’ve yet to try the sushi though, so maybe thats good? Service tends to be slow but this is difficult since they’re always busy. Sometimes it can take up to 30 minutes to receive your food after you order.

reviews.author: Moonfall Rosa
reviews.text: I recently visited on the 19th September, me and my partner had been looking forward to visiting after a wonderful visit to Manchester's last year, we booked a table ahead and arrived ten minutes ahead and were seated. However we were not impressed by the service sadly. Firstly as we were greeted the server seemed completely unenthusastic, sighing and banging the drum in passing which at that point why bother doing it if Ur not going to do it properly. I thought, fair enough, maybe they've had a bad night, a bad shift can really stink. However we were seated, it was all clean, that was no issue, but right away our server was hovering behind my partner waiting for us to pick what to have which made us feel rushed, would come to ask and we would say oh we've just sat down we haven't really had a chance to read the menu yet, mind you I'm not exaggerating, we sat down no more than 15 seconds ago. We then are looking through the menu and I kept glancing up to our waitress (a south Asian woman) because she was hovering and looking at us impatiently leaving us quite stressed as we tried to decide what to have. We chose drinks, they took a while to come out, but it wasn't terrible. Then eventually the food was ordered, the whole time the waitress was just silently hovering and glaring and felt quite intimidating, I don't really care about a waiter asking if we are ready to order yet since of course they have to ask, but we would be making a point of exaggerating we were reading and indecisive so she would relax and stop breathing down our necks but she wouldn't go, and asked us probably 5 times in the span of a couple minutes if we were ready. Eventually we ordered food (within about 10 minutes of being there) and then we waited almost an hour for the food to be ready, multiple tables who arrived after us and ordered after us got their food first, mind you they were also couples so 2 person tables and both also getting the same sort of order, two ramens. We were not apologised to for the wait and we tried to just let it go and enjoy the food because again peopl can just be having a bad day. However this experience has stayed with me and whole the food was delicious, I really can't help but think to the hour long wait for the food, the restaurant was not completely full, so I do not know if maybe an earlier rush had the staff/chefs exhausted or running low on certain stock. If this was the case I would love if in the future there could be a "this dish will take a bit longer to make, approx X amount of time" or even just to not have the waitress so persistent and in a foul mood the entire time. Even throughout the meal, she seemed to come over and just stand over us. Not asking us "how is your food?" (Which I genuinely prefer when that doesn't happen), but just standing and I'd keep glancing and she would just be glaring. I get people can have a bad day but it really ruined the dinner, I couldn't just have a nice experience and relax and enjoy the lovely food, I felt tense and on edge being watched the whole time. We had a service charge added on the bill which we didn't ask to be removed because we felt a bit intimidated and awkward but I certainly wouldn't have paid it given the choice. This should be a yes or no box to tick or press rather than automatically applying. The service didn't need to be exceptional above and beyond. Just not miserable, moody, glaring, intimidating.

reviews.author: Aliya Khan
reviews.text: If i could give a 0, I would. The service at maki and ramen Leeds by the tall south asian guy and the south asian woman is appalling. I came with a leg injury on my right knee, i requested a booth so I wouldnt be bumping and further injuring my leg due to the ridiculously small tables they provide for two people. They were very weird about giving away booth tables “in case someone else came” (even though the restaurant was mostly empty). They said we could only get a booth table if we booked in advance so we came another time with a booking. But they refused to give a table again. When we did manage to eat, the South Asian woman demanded I throw away my leftovers, even though we tidied up the table for them. What’s the point in paying service charge for such poor service?? The staff also seem to work in fear of the tyrannical stuck up south Asian guy. We were loyal customers but due to the circumstances given we won’t be returning to the leeds branch. The customer service ruins an otherwise beautiful restaurant.

And on a small table everything just felt jammed on. We had the pumpkin fritters type things and the gyoza which were nice the pumpkin thing was really nice and worth the money .. I had the seafood hellfire. That were the thought of something nice ended. The squid was tough and extremely chewy and felt horrible, the broth when I asked what meat is the broth made out of they told me they only use vegetable broth which was disappointing... The thin strips of grilled salmon was nice but due to how thin they were is was very crispy and hard. The prawns were NOT deveined. So I had a mouthful of grit and extras..... The noodle was not nice..... Overall the dish lacked proper flavour. My beautiful wife had a chicken yakisobi and she experienced a similar result. They automatically add a discretionary service charge. I don't mind actually paying for a good service but a normal standard service should be included. So again I was disappointed..... After a meal and starter each and 2 drinks we were £70+ light and disappointed.... Never will we return but on good news the post it's on the wall was great and I like the idea.

reviews.text: Disappointed Service. I visited Meadowhall branch at opening time on 24 September 2026. The restaurant was very quiet, with hardly any customers. The lunch menu was sitting at the front where the staff kept the menus to bring out to customers, but we were only given the regular menu and nobody mentioned the lunch menu. When we asked about the lunch menu, the male staff member only then brought it over. He also seemed very indifferent and dismissive when we asked questions, which made us feel quite unwelcome. When we paid, the staff member processed the payment without saying anything and simply walked away. There was no "all done", "thank you" or even an indication that the payment was complete, so we didn't even realise we had finished paying and awkwardly left. I've also visited one of London branches with my children. Despite being much busier, the staff there were much friendlier and more welcoming. I initially sent this feedback by email to info@makiramen.com on the same day we visited, but received no response, so l've decided to share my experience here instead.

reviews.text: I was appalled with the level of customer service there was. Not only we were giving our drinks AFTER our food was served and eaten, we saw the table next to us being seated down after us and given their drinks before us. There was an incident where I asked for the bill by I assumed was the manager on duty, and she said that there was a delay as they had to print out 8 bills and the receipt machine was having problems, we waited roughly 20-25 minutes without any communications while the blonde lady looked at us a lot, we then saw the table next to us asking for the bill and immediately got their receipt even though we waited for some times. I told the other waiter that we have been waited for ages and I told the lady we needed the bill and he said “oh” without any apologies on her behalf which makes us believe they did not really care about our time.

reviews.text: First time visiting with my siblings, we brought in drinks from outside, as we didn’t see the sign on the outside saying no drinks from outside. We were told this by the staff which we understood, we put the drinks away after being told and didn’t bring them out after. However if you are going to impose this rule then at least bring out the water we requested when we ordered the meal. All our food came out but the water didn’t. Lacking in customer servicing when you were happy to tell us to put the drinks away but we’re not providing us water when asked during order taking. Nonetheless the food was good the sushi was nice and the beef ramen was good, the chicken however was bland. Looking at other reviews, I can see people had similar issues. Atmosphere is nice and calm, chill and the decor is beautiful, especially the post stick note wall.

reviews.text: I guess this is the worst Japanese restaurant I’ve ever been. The tuna and white fish were fishy and I even accidentally swallowed a bone from the nigiri. The rice was bland and cold, even worse than takeaway sushi. I have to say the atmosphere was good and chill. However, I realized the floor and sushi bar were quite dirty. Overall, I’d rather go to Eat Tokyo on the next street, cheaper and better food.

reviews.author: Rayn Chan
reviews.text: Poor imitation of omakase What is japanese food? I can't say i know it all, but this place certainly knows nothing. Firstly, their signature 'hand roll'. If you have had any experience with sushi before you will know that temaki is supposed to be ice cream cone shaped with lots of rice and sashimi on top - the point for it being a filling snack/starter. However, their ones were small (it already looks small enough but when you grab it you can feel that its not even filled with rice) and then they tried to impress me by saying some fancy words, even though with it being called negitoro (shredded fatty tuna) it was just normal thin supermarket tuna. Poor fish got slaughtered just to be put in that trash then fell out because it wasnt even rolled tight enough. Secondly, the service. Its so obvious that they prioritize looks over quality (classic tourist scam) but they don't even give you any water, soysauce plate or wasabi despite it appearing as a fancy cuisine. When the food was served the waitress had a dead look on her face and mumbled the names of the sashimi really quickly. I might have wrote alot already, but guess what? Theres still more. I'll just bullet point them. • Cheap supermarket soysauce and wasabi • Putting avocado in sushi • Most customers were european people (not being racist) who came for instagram posts, showing what kind of people would actually come to this place. • No actual asian chefs • Expensive ( £10 + for just some cheap tuna and £30 for a plate of miniature sashimi) The only good things were that the food didn't take that long to arrive and i guess the beard guy was chill. If you want actual authentic japanese food, don't come here. I'd recommend RAI which is nearby and sells the same thing.
